fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/run passes, with a new test in internal/run/store_test.go that can only pass with the on-disk cache: with t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", t.TempDir()) and t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir()) so no test reads the host's user cache, List once over a store, append to one journal, then clear the process-wide journalCache and List again over a fresh Store; journalReads counts only the appended journal, the result equals an uncached List, and the cache file lies under the test-set cache dir, not the repository or .rhiza. Checks: block gives RHIZA_CPUPROFILE=$TMPDIR/inbox.prof $TMPDIR/rhiza-x inbox in the main checkout (one warm call first) before and after, with go tool pprof -top -cum showing run.(*Store).List's share fall, and /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' of the warm call both times. go test -trimpath -count=1 -p 2 ./internal/api -run 'Inbox' passes. Failure case, same setup (test-set XDG_CACHE_HOME and HOME, process-wide journalCache cleared, fresh Store): a cache file that is corrupt or from another format version is ignored and every journal is parsed (journalReads equals the journal count), with List equal to an uncached List (tested in internal/run/store_test.go)
fields.files: internal/run/store.go, internal/run/store_test.go, internal/api/inbox.go only where it calls rs.List
fields.must_not: Change the run journal's file format or what List returns; write the cache under the repository or .rhiza; read the host's real user cache in a test; serve a changed journal from the cache
fields.statement: rhiza inbox reads the run journals that changed since its last call and reuses, from a cache in the user cache folder keyed by each journal's path, size and modification time, what it parsed of the rest, so run.Store.List's share of an inbox call falls to the journals that changed

Checks: block gives, before and after, /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %U user %S sys' go test -trimpath -count=1 -cpuprofile $TMPDIR/ship.prof ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/run-ship' with the go tool pprof -top -cum lines of the cost cut, the after run's user+sys CPU below the before's; and /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %U user %S sys' go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/api ./cmd/rhiza ./internal/index run once at the commit and once in a git worktree at the change set's base 5d2596d under $TMPDIR, back to back: the commit's wall time at most 60% (240 s / 400 s) of the base's, cmd/rhiza's own package time (its go test ok line) at most 60% of the base's, and the commit's user+sys CPU at most 60% of the base's as a further check, both runs' wall, CPU and per-package times in the Checks: block. The full cold make test against m39-cold's 240 s is the milestone's own measurement, taken after the change set lands, not by the run. fields.statement: The cold suite's critical path shortens: cmd/rhiza's run-ship scripts (run-ship-ci-fix, run-ship-conflict-fix, run-ship-conflict-fix-more, run-ship-change-rebase, run-ship-model-conflict, run-ship-land-conflict and run-ship-change, about 95 s of the 864 script-seconds in cmd/rhiza/testdata/script-timings.tsv) stop paying for the top cost a go test -cpuprofile of them names outside the commands they check after scripts-top-cost-cut, cut in cmd/rhiza's test harness; and once api-tests-copy-prebuilt-index and scripts-top-cost-cut have landed with it, a cold run of the three slowest packages is within m39-cold's 240 s target in proportion: its wall time, and cmd/rhiza's own package time, at most 240/400 of the base's

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -count=1 -p 2 ./internal/api -run 'Inbox' passes, plus go test -trimpath -count=1 for each of internal/index and internal/model the cut touches. Checks: block gives RHIZA_CPUPROFILE of a warm $TMPDIR/rhiza-x inbox built at the parent commit (the three inbox leaves landed) and at the commit, with the pprof -top -cum lines of each cost cut, their share falling; and $TMPDIR/rhiza-base, built at the change set's base 5d2596d (a git worktree under $TMPDIR), and $TMPDIR/rhiza-x, built at the commit, run alternately five times each back to back in the main checkout after one warm call of each, each run's user+sys CPU taken from /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %U user %S sys' for rhiza inbox, the median of $TMPDIR/rhiza-x's at most 31% (200 ms / 645 ms) of the median of $TMPDIR/rhiza-base's.
